claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 3.0, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 3.01 to 3.03 (change +0.02).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 3.01 to 0.13. Changed by strict mode: fields eps_reported.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.94 (as submitted, 5 bps: 3.01); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 3.01 against 3.01 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 0.67 against 3.01 in research, a gap of +2.35.
The best year gives 15% of total P&L (year 5) and calm regimes give 82%; Sharpe is 3.6 in calm and 1.85 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 3.00 becomes 3.00 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 3.08 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.54).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 19% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 11% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
